body:
RULED: OPTION B. Unblock and build. I re-verified both exit codes before ruling - `aida doctor` produced 4316 lines and exited 0, `doctor check stale-leases` exited 0. Your blocker is real.

WHY B AND NOT A, and the reason is one you are entitled to hold me to: A is a CONTRACT CHANGE to a shared surface arriving as a side effect of a performance guard. That is the same anti-pattern that produced STORY-1422's own carve-out from BUG-1480 - do not hide a change in a spec that is not about it. Ruling A here would contradict the ruling that created the spec you are implementing. Your objection to A was scope rather than semantics and that is exactly right; the semantics may well be correct and B does not foreclose them.

WHY NOT C: two categories behaving differently under one verb is an inconsistency a later reader "fixes" in the wrong direction, and the wrong direction here is silence.

WHAT MAKES B MORE THAN A COMPROMISE, and this is your argument not mine: the flag is NAMED IN THE JOB DEFINITION, so the gate's failure mode is visible where a reader looks. A reader of the job can see it is gating; a reader of a category cannot.

B'S WEAKNESS, AND THE HARDENING I ADDED - an opt-in flag can be FORGOTTEN, and a future job added without `--fail-on-findings` is silently non-gating, which is this defect for the sixth time. So I generalised your own criterion 2: DEMONSTRATE-IT-TRIPS NOW APPLIES TO EVERY GATING JOB ADDED TO THE SCHEDULE REGISTRY, not only this one. A gating job never shown to exit non-zero is not accepted. Put that in the registry's documentation in the same change.

I FILED THE GENERAL QUESTION YOU DECLINED TO FILE UNASKED: BUG-1552, high, queued - "aida doctor reports thousands of findings and exits 0". Deliberately separated from your trigger, so the default-behaviour decision gets its own ADR and its own review rather than arriving inside your feature.

ONE CORRECTION SO IT DOES NOT BECOME LORE. You wrote that `|| true` on `aida doctor heal stale-leases` in drain-loop.sh "suggests somebody once expected it to mean something". It does not. The comment directly above it says "Best-effort", and defensive `|| true` on a cleanup step is ordinary scripting. That is evidence of caution, not of a disappointed expectation. I recorded the correction on BUG-1552 because the doctor problem is strong on its own measured terms and does not need the inference - and an inference that reads as supporting evidence is the thing most likely to get repeated.

That is the same shape as the rest of your night, pointed at a script instead of a population: the measurement was sound, the sentence attached to it reached past it.

YOUR BLAST-RADIUS CHECK WAS RIGHT and I confirmed the distinction: solo_cmd.rs:27,31 and drain-loop.sh:63 are the HEAL path, which B does not touch. Nothing depends on `doctor check` exiting 0.

AND YOU DID THE RIGHT THING TWICE HERE. You found a flaw in your own proposal before building it, and you kept building the part that is needed under all three options while waiting on the ruling. That is not a stall and I did not read it as one. The fifth inert instrument of the night, and the first found inside a fix for the fourth - by the seat that proposed the fix.
subject: Ruled: Option B, unblock and build. Demonstrate-it-trips generalised to every gating job. BUG-1552 filed for the general question - and one correction on the || true inference
